cand.title: CGNA2027 — 24th Biennial Conference
cand.organizationName: Canadian Gerontological Nursing Association and Gerontological Nursing Association Ontario
cand.excerpt: Ranked on verified event/date/venue and plausible multi-day professional demand, with a penalty for committed venues and absent room-block evidence.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two named referral candidates, not two verified hotel buyers: Anthony Lombardo, CGNA association management, is the strongest administrative routing contact; Julie Rubel is identified in the 2026 nomination notice as CGNA Past President and Nominating Committee Chair. Neither source establishes 2027 hotel-contract or conference-purchasing authority. Use the published event inbox conference@cgna.net to request the accommodation/ancillary-event decision-maker rather than presenting either person as the confirmed buyer.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming and within the requested horizon: May 5–7, 2027, Hart House, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. These are activity dates, not publication dates: May 5 pre-conference workshops and delegates’ reception; May 6–7 main sessions; May 6 networking event. No post-2027 edition announcement was located; do not manufacture 2029 dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment using the supplied hotel specifications: a 157-room Harbourfront city hotel could serve a subset of delegates, speakers or executives and small ancillary meetings, but there is no verified room requirement to underwrite a block. Expected attendance is 200–300; the supplied approximately 240-theatre/224-banquet ballroom limit does not safely support a full-attendance 300-person plenary or banquet, and the main venue is already Hart House. Do not convert attendees into guestrooms or presume the hotel can house everyone. The venue is not in the hotel’s immediate Harbourfront/MTCC cluster; transport convenience must be tested. This is a city-conference lodging proposition, not a sourced resort requirement. The official hotel page states “Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice”; catering/reception operation must be separately confirmed before selling it.
findings.venueCommitments: The edition-specific official site names Hart House, University of Toronto; its address is 7 Hart House Circle, Toronto, Ontario M5S 3H3. This is Toronto proper, downtown university/St George campus, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. Hart House is the published conference venue, not a competing hotel. Public naming establishes the announced venue, not access to the signed venue contract or its cancellation terms.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified destinations vary: Calgary 2019; online 2021 after Niagara Falls had originally been planned; Niagara Falls 2023; Winnipeg 2025; Toronto 2027. This supports a biennial, multi-destination series, not an annual Toronto account. Historical hotel usage is not evidence of uncommitted 2027 inventory. The exact 2023 venue remains unverified.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific incumbent: DoubleTree by Hilton Toronto Downtown, 108 Chestnut Street, Toronto, is the only hotel named on the reviewed 2027 travel/FAQ pages. Travel page quote: “Conference Hotel” and “Starting from $269/night + tax”; FAQ quote: “Reduced hotel rates are available at the Doubletree By Hilton Hotel Toronto Downtown.” The travel page describes a 20-minute walk to Hart House. This is an official conference-hotel/rate arrangement, not a generic preferred-hotel recommendation. No public 2027 allocation, peak rooms, total room nights, cutoff, reservation mechanism, housing bureau or open hotel RFP was found. The 2025 Fort Garry block must not be carried forward to 2027.
findings.organizationStructure: Association-led conference jointly hosted by the Canadian Gerontological Nursing Association and Gerontological Nursing Association Ontario. CGNA describes a volunteer-driven board. Anthony Lombardo’s profile identifies an association-management role and presidency of The Lombardo Group Incorporated; this does not establish that firm as the appointed CGNA2027 PCO. Hart House is the venue; DoubleTree is the conference hotel; neither is identified as the event owner. No appointed housing bureau, PCO or DMC was verified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Hart House has the published main-program venue position and DoubleTree has the published official hotel/rate position. There is no sourced evidence of sold-out accommodation, a full block, mandated overflow, exclusivity, attrition or permission to add a second hotel. Published 200–300 expected attendees are not confirmed room demand. Radisson should not displace the named venue/hotel in the opportunity record or describe this as open sourcing.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: First send a short, non-displacement enquiry to conference@cgna.net, for the attention of Anthony Lombardo/association management, requesting the named 2027 accommodation and ancillary-event lead. Acknowledge Hart House and DoubleTree; ask whether an approved secondary lodging option, speaker rooms or a small unplaced side meeting is actually needed, and whether incumbent terms permit it. Request required nights, pickup/peak rooms, budget and transport expectations before pricing. Do not offer a speculative 15–109-room block or catering package. Internally verify restaurant/lounge and event-catering operation. If 2027 is closed, ask for the next destination-selection and hotel-sourcing timetable, without assuming a Toronto return.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 is confirmed, but the core meeting venue and official conference-hotel route are already named. Commercial inference: accessibility is limited to organizer-approved secondary accommodation, speaker/VIP lodging or genuinely unplaced ancillary meetings. None of those needs is confirmed. The May 5 reception and May 6 networking event are already listed as programme activities; their appearance is not an external catering RFP.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: The biennial series and varied historical destinations support relationship development for a future Toronto return or smaller association meetings, not a confirmed subsequent Toronto edition. A later cycle would be competitive capture only after destination, scale, requirements and sourcing timetable are established. No post-2027 dates, city, venue or hotel competition are verified.
